name: Cosmic microwave background observation
description: Penzias and Wilson reported an unexpected microwave excess later interpreted with the Princeton team as cosmic background radiation.

impact.note: The discovery itself, not a showing of something known: cosmologists gained direct evidence of a hot early universe, and background-radiation measurement became a field.

date.basis: Year of the dated publication, or a broad historian-estimated composition interval; no first discovery claimed.

events.statement: Penzias and Wilson published the excess radio-temperature observation in 1965; a Princeton group supplied a contemporaneous cosmological interpretation.

evidence.supports: Penzias identifies his Bell Labs observation with Wilson, the 1965 paper, and the repurposed antenna.
